st: Heat [[3 tbsp]] lard or oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onions for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in [[3 tbsp]] paprika right away so it does not burn.
Add the beef, garlic, [[1 tsp]] caraway, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Return to medium heat and stir 5 minutes.
Pour in [[8 cup]] water and bring to a boil.
Reduce to low, cover and simmer for 1.5 hours until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the carrots, bell pepper and tomato and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook 20 minutes more until tender.
Taste, adjust the salt, and serve hot with crusty bread.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a wide pot and brown the chicken skin side down for 5 minutes per side. Set aside.
Cook the onions in the same pot for 8 minutes until soft.
Remove from heat, stir in [[3 tbsp]] paprika, then add the bell pepper and tomato.
Return the chicken, add [[1 cup]] stock and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cover and simmer 30 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Whisk [[1 tbsp]] flour into [[0.75 cup]] sour cream, then stir in a ladle of hot sauce to temper it.
Stir the sour cream mixture into the pot over low heat and warm for 3 minutes without boiling.
Boil the noodles per the package and serve the chicken and sauce over them.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] lard or oil in a heavy pot over medium-low heat and cook the onions for 12 minutes until very soft.
Remove from the heat and stir in [[3 tbsp]] paprika.
Add the beef, garlic, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and stir to coat.
Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring, until the meat releases juices.
Add the bell pepper, tomatoes and [[1 cup]] water. Cover.
Simmer on low for 1.5 to 2 hours, adding a splash of water if it gets dry, until the beef is tender and the sauce is thick.
Serve with egg dumplings, noodles, or boiled potatoes and pickles.

ing: cut in chunks, bones for stock if possible
st: Put [[6 cup]] water and the chopped onions in a large pot. Add fish heads or bones if you have them.
Bring to a boil and cook 30 minutes. Strain through a sieve, pressing the onions, and return the broth to the pot.
Stir [[3 tbsp]] sweet paprika and [[1 tsp]] hot paprika into the broth with [[2 tsp]] salt.
Add the bell pepper and tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
Gently lay the fish chunks in the broth. Do not stir, but shake the pot.
Simmer 12 to 15 minutes until the fish flakes.
Taste, add more salt or hot paprika, and serve with bread.
Cook the onion in [[2 tbsp]] oil for 5 minutes, then stir in [[1 tbsp]] paprika and cool.
Mix the onion with [[1.5 lb]] pork, [[0.5 cup]] rice, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Trim the thick rib from each cabbage leaf. Put a spoonful of filling in each leaf, fold in the sides and roll up tight.
Spread half of the [[2 cup]] sauerkraut in a large pot and add the sliced sausage.
Pack in the rolls, add [[1]] bay leaf and top with the remaining sauerkraut.
Add water to just cover, place a plate on top, and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 1.5 hours until the pork reaches at least 160°F (71°C).
Serve with a spoonful of [[0.5 cup]] sour cream over the top.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a wide pot and fry the sausage for 5 minutes until browned. Remove.
Cook the onions in the fat for 8 minutes until soft.
Take off the heat, stir in [[1 tbsp]] paprika, then add the peppers.
Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[1 tsp]] sugar and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper. Simmer 15 minutes until thick.
Return the sausage and warm through.
Crack 4 eggs on top, cover, and cook for 4 minutes until the whites are set. Serve with bread.
Mix [[0.75 cup]] warm milk, [[1 tsp]] sugar and [[2.25 tsp]] yeast and wait 5 minutes until foamy.
Stir in [[3 cup]] flour, the mashed potato and [[1.5 tsp]] salt to form a soft dough.
Knead 8 minutes until smooth and slightly sticky.
Cover and let rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 4 balls and flatten each into a round about 7 inches wide, thin in the middle.
Heat [[3 cup]] oil in a wide pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry one at a time for 2 minutes per side until puffed and golden.
Drain and rub with crushed garlic from [[2 clove]].
Top with [[0.5 cup]] sour cream and [[1 cup]] cheese and eat hot.
Boil potatoes in salted water for 25 minutes until just tender. Peel when cool enough and slice thinly.
Boil 6 eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and slice.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and butter a 9 by 13 inch dish using [[1 tbsp]] butter.
Layer half the potatoes, season with [[0.75 tsp]] salt and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper.
Add half the eggs and half the sausage, then spread with [[0.5 cup]] sour cream.
Repeat the layers, ending with potatoes. Spread [[1 cup]] sour cream on top.
Sprinkle with [[0.25 cup]] bread crumbs if using, and dot with [[2 tbsp]] butter.
Bake 35 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest 10 minutes.

ing: farmer cheese or dry curd works best
st: Boil the noodles in water with [[1 tbsp]] salt for 8 minutes, then drain.
Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes until crisp.
Add the drained noodles to the bacon and its fat, and toss for 2 minutes.
Warm [[0.75 cup]] sour cream until loose and stir in [[0.25 tsp]] pepper.
Dollop [[1.5 cup]] cottage cheese and the sour cream over the noodles and serve hot.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Trace six 8 inch circles on parchment and flip over onto sheet pans.
Beat 6 egg yolks with [[0.5 cup]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] vanilla until pale, about 4 minutes.
In a clean bowl beat 6 egg whites with a pinch of salt until foamy, then add [[0.5 cup]] sugar and beat to stiff peaks.
Fold the whites into the yolks in two parts, then fold in [[1 cup]] flour.
Spread thin layers into each circle and bake 6 minutes each until pale golden. Cool.

Melt [[8 oz]] chocolate gently and cool slightly. Beat [[1 cup]] butter with [[1 cup]] powdered sugar and 4 extra yolks, then beat in the chocolate. The yolks are raw, so use pasteurized if concerned.
Sandwich five layers with buttercream and spread the sides and top with the rest.
Boil [[0.75 cup]] sugar with [[3 tbsp]] water until amber, about 8 minutes. Pour over the sixth layer, mark 12 slices immediately with an oiled knife, then top the cake.
Chill 2 hours before serving.
Mix [[1 cup]] warm milk, [[0.5 cup]] sugar and [[2.25 tsp]] yeast and rest 5 minutes.
Add 2 eggs, [[3.5 cup]] flour, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.25 cup]] melted butter. Knead 10 minutes.
Cover and rise 1 hour until doubled.
Roll the dough into a rectangle about 12 by 18 inches and cut into ribbons about 1 inch wide.
Wrap each ribbon around a greased rolling pin or foil-covered cylinder, overlapping slightly.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Brush with some of the remaining [[0.25 cup]] butter and roll in a mix of [[0.75 cup]] sugar and [[1 tbsp]] cinnamon.
Bake, rotating every 10 minutes, for 30 minutes until the sugar caramelizes.
Roll in [[0.5 cup]] chopped walnuts, slide off the form and serve warm.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a 9 inch pan with parchment.
Beat 4 yolks with [[0.25 cup]] sugar until thick. Beat 4 whites with a pinch of salt and [[0.25 cup]] sugar to stiff peaks.
Fold the whites into the yolks, then fold in [[0.75 cup]] flour. Bake 20 minutes and cool.
Make a second sponge the same way, folding in [[1 tbsp]] cocoa. Bake and cool.
Cut the sponges into cubes and layer in a large dish with [[0.5 cup]] walnuts and [[0.25 cup]] raisins.
Simmer [[0.25 cup]] sugar with [[0.5 cup]] water and [[2 tbsp]] rum for 3 minutes. Drizzle over the sponge.
Heat [[0.75 cup]] cream, pour over [[6 oz]] chocolate and stir until smooth. Pour over the cake.
Whip the remaining [[0.75 cup]] cream and spread on top. Chill 1 hour before serving.
Rub [[0.5 cup]] cold butter into [[3 cup]] flour with your fingertips until crumbly. Stir in [[1 tsp]] yeast and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Add [[0.5 cup]] sour cream, the egg yolk and [[0.5 cup]] grated cheese. Mix just until it forms a dough.
Roll out to 1 inch thick on a floured counter. Fold into thirds, turn and roll again. Repeat twice for flaky layers.
Chill the dough for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 400°F.
Roll to 0.75 inch thick and score a diamond pattern with a knife. Cut into 2 inch rounds.
Brush with beaten egg, top with remaining [[0.5 cup]] cheese and bake 18 to 20 minutes until golden.
nt: Best swap: Greek yogurt can replace sour cream at the same amount.

st: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 25 minutes until tender. Peel while hot, then mash smooth and spread out to cool for 15 minutes.
Mix the potatoes with the flour, egg and salt. Knead lightly into a soft dough and add flour a spoonful at a time if sticky.
Cut each plum along one side, remove the pit and press in a sugar cube.
Pinch off a piece of dough, flatten it in your palm, wrap it around a plum and roll into a smooth ball with no gaps.
Bring a wide pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Add the dumplings in batches and cook 12 minutes, until they float and the dough is cooked.
Melt the butter in a skillet, toast the breadcrumbs for 4 minutes until golden, then stir in the sugar and cinnamon.
Roll the drained dumplings in the crumbs. Serve warm.
nt: Boiled, then rolled in toasted crumbs
Best swap: use apricots in place of plums with a sugar cube for a Marillagombóc, same amount.

st: Put the cherries, water, sugar, cinnamon stick, cloves, lemon zest and salt in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes until the cherries are soft.
Whisk the flour into the sour cream in a bowl until smooth. Slowly whisk in [[1 cup]] of the hot cherry liquid to temper it.
Remove the cinnamon stick and cloves from the pot. Turn the heat to low and pour the cream mixture in, stirring constantly.
Heat for 3 minutes without boiling so the cream does not split, then taste and add sugar if the cherries are very tart.
Cool to room temperature, then chill in the fridge for at least 3 hours until very cold. Serve in chilled bowls.
nt: Simmered fruit, thickened with sour cream, served chilled
Best swap: use frozen or jarred sour cherries drained 1:1; for dairy-free use coconut yogurt in place of sour cream.

st: Heat the oven to 325°F. Trace five 8 inch circles on parchment sheets and flip them over onto baking trays.
Whip the egg whites to soft peaks, then add [[0.75 cup]] sugar a spoonful at a time until the meringue is stiff and glossy.
Fold in the walnuts and [[2 tbsp]] flour gently so the foam does not deflate.
Spread the batter thinly inside each circle and bake for 20 minutes until pale gold and dry. Peel off the paper while warm and cool flat.
For the cream, whisk the yolks, milk and remaining [[0.25 cup]] sugar over low heat for 8 minutes until it reaches 160°F and coats a spoon. Cool completely.
Beat the softened butter until fluffy, then beat in the cooled custard and vanilla a spoonful at a time until smooth.
Stack the layers with buttercream between them, keeping the best layer for the top. Spread the sides with the remaining cream and chill 1 hour.
Warm the jam and brush it over the top. Mix the powdered sugar with a little warm water to a thick glaze and spread it on top.
Pipe thin lines of melted chocolate across the glaze, then drag a toothpick across them in alternating directions for the feathered pattern. Chill before slicing.
nt: Baked at 325°F, then layered and chilled
Best swap: ground almonds or hazelnuts in equal amounts if you do not have walnuts.

st: Place the plums, sugar, cinnamon stick, cloves and [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Cook for 20 minutes, stirring, until the plums release juice and soften.
Lower the heat and cook uncovered for 2 hours, stirring every 10 minutes so it does not scorch, until dark and thick.
Remove the cinnamon stick and cloves. Blend smooth with an immersion blender if you prefer.
The lekvar is ready when a spoon dragged across the pot leaves a clear track. Cook 10 minutes more if not.
Ladle into clean jars, cool, and chill. Use on pancakes, in pastries or on bread.
nt: Slowly simmered on the stove until thick
Best swap: dried prunes soaked in hot water for 1 hour if fresh plums are out of season.

st: Season the chicken with salt. Heat [[3 tbsp]] lard in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and sear the chicken 5 minutes per side until golden. Remove.
Cook the onions in the same pot over medium heat for 10 minutes until very soft and golden.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in [[3 tbsp]] paprika so it does not scorch and turn bitter, then add the broth, tomato and green pepper.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer gently for 40 minutes until it reads 175°F.
Whisk the flour into the sour cream, then stir in a ladle of hot sauce. Pour back into the pot and warm 3 minutes without boiling.
Serve over cooked egg noodles with the sauce.
nt: Seared, then braised on the stove
Best swap: use full-fat Greek yogurt in place of sour cream at the same ratio, and bring it to room temperature.

st: Melt the lard in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the paprika, then return it. Paprika burns quickly, so stir right away.
Add the sausage, pepper and tomato and cook 3 minutes.
Add the potatoes, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[2 cups]] water, enough to just cover. Bring to a boil.
Reduce to a simmer, cover partly, and cook 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the broth is thick.
Serve hot with a spoonful of sour cream if you like.
nt: Best swap: use sunflower oil and skip the sausage, adding 0.5 tsp smoked paprika for a vegetarian version.
